browser_repost_prompt_humility_note: Generic browser repost prompts are treated as residual browser behavior rather than as office-controlled proof of receipt or duplicate protection.
delivery_role_note: After a voter submits a state-changing request, the service lands on a reviewable confirmation or status route instead of treating a browser repost prompt as the confirmation surface.
duplicate_retry_boundary_note: The route distinguishes already received, safe to retry, duplicate-risk, and unknown-outcome states in ordinary page copy.
external_handoff_boundary_note: Cross-origin or third-party handoffs are reviewed separately from this post-submit browser-state control.
long_running_status_route_note: When final resolution is not immediate, the service redirects to a truthful status/help lane instead of implying that processing is complete.

post_submit_destination_classes.class_note: After acceptance, the voter lands on a GET-retrievable confirmation page that can be refreshed without replaying the original submit.
Longer-running review paths land on a current status page rather than leaving the voter on a browser repost-risk shell.

post_submit_redirect_surface_label: Example post-submit redirect and refresh-safe confirmation posture for official voter-information routes
redirect_semantics_boundary_note: Redirect posture is reviewed explicitly after submit so routes do not quietly rely on ambiguous or method-preserving redirects when the public promise is a safe confirmation page.
refresh_safe_confirmation_note: Reviewed routes that promise confirmation or status land on refresh-safe retrieval pages rather than on residual POST result shells.
safe_retry_or_help_note: Each reviewed submit route keeps a bounded confirmation/status/help recovery path for uncertain outcomes.
